_comment: TODO-009's acceptance gate, written BEFORE normalize_ar existed — which is
the point. Arabic search without normalization looks like it works and
quietly misses: a user types محمد, the record says مُحَمَّد, and they get zero
results with no error and no signal that anything went wrong. F206 names
Arabic as the moat, so this table is what that claim is measured against.
Each group is a set of strings that MUST all normalize to the same value.
`normalized` is the expected output, asserted absolutely — a group that only
asserted 'these are equal to each other' would pass if normalize_ar returned

groups.name: tashkeel (harakat) are stripped
groups.why: Diacritics are optional in written Arabic. A name typed without them must match a record that has them, and vice versa — this is the single most common Arabic search miss.

groups.name: tatweel (kashida) is removed
groups.why: U+0640 is a purely typographic stretch character used for justification. It carries no meaning and must never affect matching.

groups.name: alef forms fold to bare alef
groups.why: أ إ آ ٱ are routinely typed as ا. Folding them is what makes احمد find أحمد.

groups.name: alef maksura folds to ya
groups.why: ى and ي are interchanged constantly in practice, including by native typists.

groups.name: taa marbuta folds to haa
groups.why: ة is commonly typed ه, especially word-final in informal input.

groups.name: hamza carriers fold
groups.why: ؤ ئ ء are inconsistently typed. Folding to the bare carrier keeps مسؤول findable as مسءول or مسئول.

groups.name: Arabic-Indic digits fold to ASCII
groups.why: An invoice number typed ١٢٣ must find a record storing 123. Both Arabic-Indic (U+0660) and Eastern Arabic-Indic (U+06F0) ranges are in use across the GCC.

groups.name: mixed Arabic and English is preserved, each normalized in place
groups.why: Mixed-language records are the GCC norm, not an edge case (P-search Q7b). The Arabic half folds and the Latin half lowercases — search is case-insensitive on both, so a group expecting ACME to survive uppercase (as this one first did) contradicts the non-Arabic group below it.

groups.name: whitespace is collapsed and trimmed
groups.why: Pasted text carries doubled spaces, tabs, and non-breaking spaces; none of them are a meaningful difference between two names.

groups.name: already-normalized text is unchanged (idempotence)
groups.why: normalize_ar runs at index time AND at query time. If it were not idempotent, a re-indexed row would drift away from the query form and matches would silently degrade over time.

groups.name: non-Arabic text passes through unchanged apart from case and whitespace
groups.why: The same function runs over every record, most of which are English. It must not mangle them.

groups.name: empty and whitespace-only input is safe
groups.why: A record with a null or blank title reaches this function like any other. It must return empty, not error and not NULL.

must_not_match.why: Normalization must not be so aggressive that distinct names collapse. These pairs are genuinely different words and must keep different normalized forms — the failure mode opposite to under-normalizing, and the one nobody tests for.
